summary: Hexaminds is a 3D space game where you run your own space missions. You get three missions: reach Earth orbit, deploy a satellite, and land on the Moon. Before every launch, you build your rocket piece by piece, picking engines, fuel tanks, cargo, satellites and nose cones. But there's a catch. You have a budget and a weight limit, so you can't just add everything. Too heavy and the rocket won't make it. Too cheap and it might fail. We made it in the Godot engine because we wanted students to feel how tricky real space missions are, and to enjoy learning it, not just read about it.
details:
Hexaminds is a 3D space mission game. The player plays as a mission planner and has to complete three missions: Earth Orbit, Satellite Deployment and Moon Landing. Before each launch, you build your own rocket from parts like engines, fuel tanks, connectors, cargo, satellites and nose cones. Every part has a price and a weight, and every mission has a limited budget. So you have to think carefully: too heavy and the rocket can't lift off, too cheap and the mission can fail.
The benefit is that players learn how space missions are planned without needing any science background. They see that rocketry is about trade-offs between cost, weight and fuel. We hope it makes students curious about space engineering and shows them it can be fun to learn.
We built it in Godot 4.7 with 3D models, and used the Orchestrator visual scripting addon for the game logic. For the menus and rocket builder screen, we first designed a prototype in HTML, CSS and JavaScript, then recreated it in Godot. Prices, weights and mission budgets are kept in simple config files, so the game is easy to edit and expand with new missions later.
It is creative because it turns rocket science into a hands-on building game. We kept the design simple for beginners, with a dark space theme in black, purple and cyan.
